speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; could you please describe exactly where the pain is located and when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis.

The history of a fall six months ago, combined with pain in the thumb and wrist radiating to the elbow that worsens with holding an infant (a classic "baby sign" for this condition), strongly suggests tendinopathy of the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis. The relief with ice and response to ibuprofen further supports an inflammatory etiology.

REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound of the right wrist to visualize tendon sheath thickening and fluid collection.
